name: metabolism-overflow
title: Does v2ecoli reproduce aerobic acetate overflow — the acetate-carbon yield vs growth rate curve?

studies.overflow-acetate-vs-growth: (baseline-FBA arm DONE 2026-07-22 — verdict mismatch, no overflow at any of 6 glucose-uptake caps; Millard / FBA-bridge arms unbuilt) Titrate the glucose-uptake cap; grade the acetate-carbon yield vs growth rate against Vemuri 2006 / Basan 2015. Two unplanned findings dominate: the knob does not move growth rate, and carbon balance fails under a binding cap.

biological_story:
When a fast-growing E. coli takes up glucose faster than its respiratory chain
can fully oxidize the carbon, it spills the excess as acetate — aerobic
"overflow" metabolism — even with oxygen present. The fraction of consumed
carbon leaving as acetate is ~0 below a critical growth rate and rises roughly
linearly above it: a clean, repeatedly-measured, strain-robust relationship
(Vemuri 2006 in chemostat; Basan 2015 by titrating glucose-transporter
expression). Basan's proteome-allocation account makes it a story about a
respiratory ceiling: past some carbon influx, respiring is more protein-expensive
per ATP than fermenting, so the cell spills.

That makes overflow an unusually good test of whether a whole-cell model encodes
a real physiological constraint rather than just a stoichiometry. A growth-max
FBA with no proteome or respiratory-capacity limit has no reason to spill carbon
— it will respire everything it takes up. So the question this investigation asks
is diagnostic, not merely comparative: drive the carbon knob, watch what comes
out, and find out WHERE the overflow physiology is or isn't encoded.

The answer for the baseline FBA arm is that it is not encoded at all: acetate is
identically zero across the whole titration. That is the expected answer, and it
localizes the gap — which is what the instrument is for.
question:
Does v2ecoli reproduce aerobic acetate overflow — the acetate-carbon yield
Y_ac = (2·acetate)/(6·glucose) rising from ~0 to ~linearly above a critical
growth rate, as measured in glucose-limited chemostat (Vemuri 2006) and batch
uptake-titration (Basan 2015) experiments — and if not, where in the model is
the overflow physiology missing?

executive.what_is_this:
A report-card investigation that grades v2ecoli's aerobic acetate-overflow
response against curated experimental curves. It titrates the model's
glucose-uptake knob, lets the phenotype emerge, and grades the resulting
acetate-carbon-yield-vs-growth-rate CURVE — shape first — against Vemuri 2006
(primary, raw yield) and Basan 2015 (context).

One study, `overflow-acetate-vs-growth`, with three planned arms: the baseline
FBA metabolism (RUN and graded), the Millard kinetic ODE, and the v2ecoli +
Millard FBA-bridge (both UNBUILT). The instrument — knob → run → extract →
grade → verdict — works end to end; what it revealed is that the experiment
design rests on an assumption v2ecoli does not satisfy.
executive.verdict_detail:
Baseline-FBA arm run and graded 2026-07-22. Verdict `mismatch`: acetate is
identically 0.0 at all six glucose-uptake caps, so the acetate-carbon yield
stays flat at 0 while the reference rises to ~0.25. That is the PREDICTED
outcome and it confirms the ketchup-baseline-comparison prior — overflow is a
constraint phenomenon, and unconstrained growth-max FBA respires fully rather
than spilling carbon.

But the run falsified this investigation's own design assumption and surfaced a
model-correctness defect, and those matter more than the verdict:

1. THE KNOB DOES NOT TITRATE GROWTH. Across a 5.6x uptake range the emergent
   growth rate moves only 0.954 -> 0.925 /h, because division fires on the
   D-period replication clock rather than on dry mass. An acetate-vs-growth-rate
   card cannot be driven by a carbon knob in this model, so the graded x-range
   is ~0.03 /h wide and the verdict rests on a degenerate sweep.
2. CARBON BALANCE FAILS UNDER A BINDING CAP, and biomass yield exceeds the
   stoichiometric ceiling at every cap.

Item 2 is NOT this investigation's to diagnose — it seeds the sibling
investigation `metabolism-biomass-yield` (v2ecoli#421), which has since run its
S1 diagnostic and resolved the one-vs-two question to TWO distinct defects.
This investigation records the observations and points there. Item 1 is a live
design question for this investigation: see the study's
`gur-knob-does-not-titrate-growth` finding.

decisions_needed.question: Does the v2ecoli baseline FBA exhibit ANY aerobic acetate overflow, or is acetate identically zero across the glucose-uptake sweep?
decisions_needed.status: RESOLVED 2026-07-22 — identically zero. Acetate = 0.0 mmol/gDCW/h at all six glucose-uptake caps (1-6); the card grades mismatch, 'no overflow'. See the study finding `overflow-absent-across-titration`.
decisions_needed.context:
The motivating prior is the ketchup-baseline-comparison characterization:
v2ecoli's baseline secretes no acetate (0.0 per 100 glucose) where the
KETCHUP cores secrete ~+71. This investigation turns that single-point
observation into a graded response curve over a glucose-uptake titration.

RESOLUTION: the prior held exactly. The baseline-FBA arm secretes no acetate
anywhere in the titration, so the single-point observation generalises to the
whole response curve. Caveat carried forward: the sweep's growth-rate axis
spans only ~0.03 /h (see `gur-knob-does-not-titrate-growth`), so this answers
"is overflow present" but not "is the overflow CURVE right". The Millard and
FBA-bridge arms remain unbuilt and unanswered.

decisions_needed.question: How should the card's x-axis be made carbon-responsive, given that the glucose-uptake knob does not move growth rate in v2ecoli?
decisions_needed.status: OPEN — the live design question for this investigation. Blocks any quantitative curve comparison; does not block the qualitative 'overflow absent' verdict already recorded.
decisions_needed.context:
Division runs with `d_period=True` (the vEcoli default), so it fires on the
D-period replication clock and the dry-mass threshold is deliberately ignored.
Mean division time — and hence the mu this study reads out — is set by
replication timing, not carbon supply. Three routes, in rough order of appeal:
re-axis the card onto the knob itself (Y_ac vs GUR, unit caveats accepted);
get a mass-gated growth mode (`d_period=False` is NOT a config flip — `division`
is absent from `_CACHE_CONFIG_NAMES`, so it is a code change); or accept the
card as a presence/absence instrument rather than a curve comparison.
Adding seeds or generations will NOT help — the axis is structurally pinned,
not noisy.

decisions_needed.question: Is the carbon-creation / yield-over-ceiling defect the same defect the basal card reports?
decisions_needed.status: RESOLVED ELSEWHERE 2026-07-29 — NO, they are two distinct defects. Owned by the sibling investigation `metabolism-biomass-yield` (v2ecoli#421), not by this one.
decisions_needed.context:
The GUR titration showed the model creating carbon under a binding cap and
biomass yield 0.92 -> 5.30 gDW/g glucose against a measured band of 0.355-0.444.
This investigation originally recorded a hypothesis that this was one defect
with the basal card's yield violation.

RESOLUTION (#421, S1 diagnostic): TWO. A fresh basal sweep shows carbon
CONSERVING at baseline (implied biomass C 0.4549 gC/gDW, RQ 3.43, O2:glucose
0.096) while yield sits 1.55x the ceiling — so the baseline defect is
ENERGETIC (the model barely respires) and is mechanistically distinct from the
carbon CREATION that appears only under a binding cap. Scope decision stands:
both are model-correctness questions, not overflow questions, and they gate
this investigation rather than depending on it — a model that creates carbon
cannot be meaningfully asked a carbon-partitioning question.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
v2ecoli's aerobic acetate-overflow response can be graded against curated
experimental curves by a shape-first, unit-invariant criterion, giving an
auditable, regression-trackable answer to "does this model overflow, and does
its overflow curve look like the measured one?" — and the same instrument
surfaces model-correctness defects that a point comparison would miss.
evidence_for: DONE (baseline-FBA arm, 2026-07-22) — a 6-point glucose-uptake titration, graded by `threshold_linear` against Vemuri 2006 (primary) / Basan 2015 (context). Verdict mismatch: acetate 0.0 at every cap, no overflow. The method works end-to-end — knob -> run -> extract -> grade -> verdict.

PARTIAL — the same run falsified the investigation's growth-rate axis (the knob does not move mu) and tripped an assumption-free carbon-creation flag, showing the report-card machinery surfaces model-correctness defects, not just agreement/disagreement with a reference.
PLANNED — the Millard kinetic-ODE and FBA-bridge arms of the same study, to test whether a kinetic central-carbon core induces the overflow the baseline FBA misses.
caveats: This is a CHARACTERIZATION (does the model reproduce the measured response?), graded as state + trend — not a model pass/fail. A model-experiment gap is a calibration target the report INVITES work on, not a defect verdict.
Resolution (recalibrating the model to close a gap) is an opportunistic follow-up study seeded from a gap finding, never a precondition of the characterization.

The recorded verdict is graded on a DEGENERATE sweep: all six points land in a ~0.03 /h growth-rate band, entirely above the reference onset. Read it as 'overflow physiology is absent', not as a quantitative curve comparison.

The carbon-balance and biomass-yield observations recorded here are NOT diagnosed here. They belong to the sibling investigation `metabolism-biomass-yield`; this investigation records them and points at it.

studies.name: overflow-acetate-vs-growth
studies.title: Does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic acetate-overflow curve (acetate-carbon yield vs growth rate) — Vemuri 2006 / Basan 2015?
studies.question:
Across a glucose-uptake-rate titration, does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic
acetate-overflow response — the acetate-carbon yield rising ~linearly with
growth rate above a critical threshold (Vemuri 2006 primary, Basan 2015
context) — and how do the FBA baseline, the Millard kinetic ODE, and the
v2ecoli+Millard FBA-bridge arms compare?

findings.statement:
The v2ecoli baseline FBA exhibits NO aerobic acetate overflow anywhere in a
glucose-uptake titration: acetate is identically 0.0 mmol/gDCW/h at all six
caps, so the acetate-carbon yield stays flat at 0 while the Vemuri 2006
reference rises to ~0.25 above an onset of 0.408 /h. This confirms the
pre-registered prediction (and the ketchup-baseline-comparison prior that
v2ecoli secretes 0.0 acetate per 100 glucose where the KETCHUP cores secrete
~+71): overflow is a constraint phenomenon, and unconstrained growth-max FBA
respires fully rather than spilling carbon.

evidence.observed: acetate 0.0 mmol/gDCW/h at caps 1,2,3,4,5,6; card verdict mismatch — 'no overflow (yield <= 0.005 through x=0.954; ref overflows)'; reference onset mu=0.408 /h, reference yield slope 1.31

expected.summary: Y_ac rising from ~0 to ~linear above the reference onset (Vemuri 2006 MG1655 chemostat, primary graded curve)

findings.next_action: Build the Millard kinetic-ODE and FBA-bridge arms to test whether a kinetic central-carbon core induces the overflow the baseline FBA misses.

findings.statement:
THIS FINDING REFUTES THIS STUDY'S OWN SECOND DESIGN ASSUMPTION — that a
glucose-uptake titration moves the model along a growth-rate axis comparable to
the references'. It is FALSE for v2ecoli. This is a refutation of our premise,
not a disagreement with a reference.

Across a 5.6x uptake range the emergent growth rate moves only 0.954 -> 0.925 /h,
non-monotonically. The cause is by design, not a bug: division runs with
d_period=True (the vEcoli default), so it fires on the D-period replication
clock and the dry-mass threshold is deliberately ignored (the `threshold=nan fg`
in every DIVISION log line; see v2ecoli/steps/division.py:181-190). Mean division
time — and hence the mu this study reads out — is therefore set by replication
timing, not carbon supply, and cells divide on schedule at ~695 fg regardless of
how tightly glucose is capped.

Consequence for the instrument: an acetate-vs-growth-rate card cannot be driven
by a carbon knob in this model. All six sweep points land in a ~0.03 /h band,
entirely above the reference onset, so the `overflow-absent-across-titration`
verdict is graded on a degenerate x-range. Adding seeds or generations will not
help — the axis is structurally pinned, not noisy.

evidence.observed: growth rate 0.954 / 0.933 / 0.924 / 0.931 / 0.927 / 0.925 per h at caps 1-6 while glucose uptake spans -1.0 to -5.59 mmol/gDCW/h (5.6x); x-range 0.030 /h vs a reference onset at 0.408 /h
evidence.smoking_gun: division.py runs d_period=True, which sets threshold=float('nan') and gates division on the replication clock rather than dry mass

findings.next_action: Decide how mu should be made carbon-responsive for perturbation cards — mass-gated division (d_period=False, accepting the early-division regression the code comment describes, and noting `division` is absent from _CACHE_CONFIG_NAMES so this is a code change not a config flip), or re-axis the card onto the knob (Y_ac vs GUR) instead of emergent growth rate.

findings.statement:
Under a binding glucose cap the model creates carbon. At cap=1 it takes up
6.0 mmolC/gDCW/h as glucose and secretes 11.83 mmolC/gDCW/h of carbon — 11.62 of
it as CO2 — while still growing at 0.954 /h and therefore also building biomass
carbon. This trips the assumption-free `violation_C_created` flag, which compares
secreted C-exchange against C uptake and needs no biomass C-content assumption.

The effect is inverted with respect to carbon supply: CO2 output RISES as glucose
is restricted (11.62 / 5.00 / 1.82 mmol/gDCW/h at caps 1 / 2 / 6), and the carbon
closure fraction degrades monotonically as the cap tightens (1.11 -> 7.93 across
caps 6 -> 1). At the slack cap the books nearly close; the tighter the constraint,
the more carbon appears from nowhere. Undiagnosed here. Candidate mechanisms: FBA
infeasibility handling under a binding bound, non-FBA replenishment of metabolite
pools, or per-gDCW flux normalisation against a stale mass.

evidence.observed: cap=1: C_in 6.0 vs C_out 11.83 mmolC/gDCW/h (violation_C_created=true); closure fraction 7.93 / 3.59 / 2.31 / 1.53 / 1.26 / 1.11 at caps 1 -> 6; CO2 11.62 / 5.00 / 1.82 at caps 1 / 2 / 6
evidence.smoking_gun: secreted carbon exceeds carbon taken up while the cell is simultaneously accumulating biomass — a mass-balance violation independent of any biomass composition assumption

expected.summary: C_out <= C_in at every cap (no carbon creation); violation_C_created false throughout

findings.next_action: Diagnosis moved OUT of this investigation 2026-07-28 — it seeds the sibling investigation `metabolism-biomass-yield` (v2ecoli#421). A model that creates carbon cannot be meaningfully asked a carbon-partitioning question, so this gates the overflow study rather than the other way round.

findings.statement:
Emergent biomass yield exceeds the stoichiometric ceiling at every cap, and the
excess grows as carbon is restricted: Yxs = 0.92 / 1.04 / 1.29 / 1.71 / 2.59 /
5.30 gDW per g glucose at caps 6 -> 1, against a measured literature band of
0.355-0.444 (Varma 1994, Kavvas 2022, LaCroix 2015, Long 2017 — the four
`kind: measured` rows of the ecoli-sources basal__biomass_yield slot) and a
stoichiometric ceiling of 0.538 (Varma 1993, the slot's single
`kind: theoretical_max` row). Even at the slack cap, where the FBA runs at its
unconstrained optimum and the carbon books nearly close, the yield is ~1.7x the
ceiling; at cap=1 it is ~10x.

This is the same defect the basal vs_literature card already reports (biomass
yield over the limit), but the titration shows it is not a fixed offset — it is
a function of how hard the carbon constraint binds, which points at the same
bookkeeping problem as `carbon-created-under-binding-uptake-cap` rather than at
a mis-parameterised biomass composition.

expected.summary: measured aerobic glucose biomass yield, ecoli-sources basal__biomass_yield slot (4 `kind: measured` sources); stoichiometric ceiling 0.538 (Varma 1993, the slot's `kind: theoretical_max` row)

findings.next_action: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-29. The former next_action — 'check whether the basal card's yield violation moves with the same knob; the two cards are likely reporting one underlying defect' — has been PERFORMED and its premise DISCONFIRMED by v2ecoli#421's S1 diagnostic (two distinct defects, not one). The live follow-up is #421's S3, scoped to maintenance-ATP / NGAM-GAM and respiratory capacity — NOT mass accounting. Nothing further is owed by this study.
